body: At 12:42 UTC, roughly 10-15 minutes after the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print, conditions remain calm and largely two-sided heading into the U.S. cash open. The S&P 500 closed Thursday at a fresh record above 7,800 on cooler-than-expected inflation data, extending a third straight weekly advance. Heading into today's session, premarket reads were mixed across indices: S&P 500 futures little changed, Dow futures down about 0.1%, and Nasdaq-100 futures up nearly 0.2% -- a modest, non-persistent tilt, not evidence of pathological directional efficiency. July Retail Sales (Census Advance Monthly, 8:30am ET / 12:30 UTC) printed within the last 10-15 minutes, but the actual headline and core figures could not be confirmed via available live sources at generation time -- search coverage of the release has not yet caught up -- so per the research contract this run treats the print as pending rather than inventing a result; consensus ahead of the release clustered around a modest +0.1-0.3% MoM headline with some analyst dispersion (one preview flagged 0.1% vs. a separate 0.3% consensus read), which itself is a mild amplifier for Stress into the cash open. VIX ticked up to 14.73 (+1.24% on the session, range 14.53-14.70 intraday per the latest read), a small but not alarming move, and the 10-year Treasury yield remains anchored near 4.65%, matching yesterday's close with no confirmed fresh print for today. Oil continues to firm on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff: WTI trades near $82.1 and Brent near $87.9 (both up modestly from the prior run's $81.3/$89.5 read, direction consistent though the WTI/Brent spread narrowed slightly across sources). The move follows U.S. officials -- including Treasury Secretary Bessent -- signaling the existing naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue 'indefinitely' and floating further 'economic isolation' measures against Iran, with reporting confirming roughly 20 additional commercial vessels were redirected away from Iranian ports over the past week. This reads as intensified rhetoric and sustained enforcement of the standing blockade rather than a new kinetic strike, vessel seizure, or full closure, so it is scored as continuation of the same protracted brinkmanship backdrop noted in prior runs, not a fresh discontinuity. The U.S. cash open (9:30am ET / 13:30 UTC) and preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment (10am ET / 14:00 UTC) are the next two checkpoints, both landing within the next 90 minutes and layering directly on top of the still-unconfirmed Retail Sales reaction. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota was already exhausted this run -- the TREASURY_YIELD call was rate-limited on both the initial attempt and an immediate retry -- so per the fallback protocol this assessment relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities, and price-path context; the inability to confirm the actual Retail Sales print this soon after release, on top of the continued Alpha Vantage outage, keeps Confidence in the low band, modestly below the prior run. Tail holds at 9% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure -- shallow/no pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or NQ holding near session extremes -- has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself; the modest +0.2% premarket futures tilt is not evidence of pathological directional efficiency, and the Retail Sales reaction has not yet been observed and scored. Stress firms to 38% (moderate, up from 33% in the prior run) reflecting the compressed event stack now directly ahead -- an unconfirmed Retail Sales reaction, the cash open, and UMich sentiment all landing within roughly the next 90 minutes -- plus the continued cross-asset tension from firmer oil against a modestly firmer VIX and flat yields, with Stress projected to build further toward the mid-40s through the cash-open/UMich window before easing back through the afternoon and into the quiet weekend handover.
